title: Understanding Principal Component Matrix
text: The principal component matrix, P, is derived from the original matrix X. It involves the singular value decomposition (SVD) of X. Can you recall what the SVD of a matrix involves?

title: Decomposing the Principal Component Matrix
text: When you decompose the principal component matrix P into its components, you are essentially performing another SVD. What are the components of an SVD?

hintAnswer: The $$3$$ by $$3$$ identity matrix, with rows (1,0,0), (0,1,0) and (0,0,1)
title: Identifying $${V_P}^T$$
text: Consider the properties of the matrices involved in the SVD. What is the role of $${V_P}^T$$ in the decomposition?
choices: The $$3$$ by $$3$$ identity matrix, with rows (1,0,0), (0,1,0) and (0,0,1)
The $$3$$ by $$3$$ matrix of all zeros, with rows (0,0,0), (0,0,0) and (0,0,0)
The $$2$$ by $$2$$ identity matrix, with rows $$(1,0)$$ and $$(0,1)$$
The same matrix as $$V^T$$ obtained from the decomposition of X
